title: The Assignment Operation
objectives: Understand what the ← assignment operator means
Read self-referencing assignments like a ← a + 1 correctly

hook.text: In math, "a = a + 1" looks impossible. In an algorithm, it is perfectly normal. Why?

concept.heading: ← reads right to left
concept.body: The statement a ← 5 does not mean "a EQUALS 5". It means "PUT the value 5 into the box a". An assignment always works out the value on the right first, then places the result in the box on the left.

captions: a ← 5 : read from right to left
the value 5 was PUT into box a

concept.heading: How does a ← a + 1 work?
concept.body: First the right side is calculated: take the CURRENT value of a and add 1. Then this new result is put back into the box a, overwriting the old value. It is not a mathematical equation, it is an UPDATE.

workedExamples.prompt: If a ← 5 and then a ← a + 1 are run, what is the final value of a?

steps.explain: 5 is put into the box a.
The right side is calculated: a (5) + 1 = 6. The result is written into a.

exercises.question: What does the statement a ← 5 mean?
options: Put the value 5 into the box a

feedback.correct: Correct. The ← operator places the value on the right into the box on the left.
feedback.incorrect: ← is an assignment, not a comparison: the value on the right is put into the box on the left.

exercises.question: How is a ← a + 1 different from the math equation "a = a + 1"?
options: There is no difference, they are the same thing
In math it is not a valid equation, but in an algorithm it is an update operation
This operation is forbidden in algorithms
In math it is always true

feedback.correct: Correct. In an algorithm, ← is not an equality, it is an update command that runs in order.
feedback.incorrect: In math a = a + 1 is impossible (it would give 0 = 1). In an algorithm it is a command that updates a.

exercises.hint: The last assigned value replaces what is in the box.

summary: The ← operator calculates the value on the right and writes it into the box on the left. It is not an equality.
a ← a + 1 reads the old value of a, adds 1, and writes the result back into a.
When a variable gets a new value, the old value is erased for good.
